newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's CSP sees Milan bourse debut around July 10.
newsitem.headline: Italy's CSP sees Milan bourse debut around July 10.

text.p: Italian hosiery company CSP International should make its Milan bourse debut around July 10, the group's director general Gianfranco Bossi said at the start of its share offer roadshow that continues into next week.
The company hopes to collect 120-150 billion lire from the share offering which will amount to between 33.6 and 40 percent of company's shares, said the lead manager of the issue Cariplo.
The share stake held by the controlling family Bertoni is set to fall to 52.2 percent from 64.1 percent, and that held by Genofin-UBS Capital down to 10.1 percent from 31.3 percent.

The group said earlier it will carry out a market share offering on June 30 and July 1 ahead of its listing on the Milan bourse. The share price, to be in a range between 12,000 and 15,000 lire, will be announced before the sale offer.
The overall offer is for 8.22 million ordinary shares of a nominal 1,000 lire each, of which 2.055 million will be offered to the public, including employees, and the rest placed privately.
CSP posted 1996 net profit of 10.5 billion lire against 2.1 billion in 1995 on sales of 233.7 billion lire versus 191.3 billion.
